messages:
maya (support): FYI customer 'Nexio' on eu2-dedicated reported sudden p95 token latency spike + bursts of 503s after an autoscale event ~09:12UTC. They also see intermittent 429s from the edge. Ticket 891234. Can eng take a look?

jason (eng-sre): Can you paste the error lines + pool/node ids? Is this a Dedicated pool (not shared)?

maya (support): Dedicated pool: eu2-dedicated-4, pool-id=ded-eu2-4, tenant=nexio. Short log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-16T09:12:13Z model-proxy ERROR request_id=abcd123 status=503 msg="model instance unavailable"
2026-03-16T09:12:13Z router WARN tenant=nexio route=/v1/generate upstream=ded-eu2-4 backend_err=429
2026-03-16T09:12:14Z runtime INFO evicting cache key=kv-xyz reason=slot-throttle
```
Also attached p95 graph (s3://…/nexio-p95-0316.png) — p50 looks fine but p95 and tail jump.

priya (eng-runtime): Do we have nvidia metrics or MIG slice allocations for that node? 503+429 pattern can be noisy-neighbor + model server restart thrash. Can you run `kubectl get pods -o wide -n pools-dedicated | grep ded-eu2-4` and `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` on the node?

infra-bot: node/ded-eu2-4-nt-03 rotated: kernel-upgrade at 09:10UTC, kubelet restarted at 09:11UTC (rotation-id=rot-2026-0316-0910).

jason (eng-sre): kernel/kubelet restart around autoscale time — could be pods rescheduled then packed coarsely. If MIG slices weren't reattached properly, two tenants could end up sharing SMs. Maya can you confirm which pods were rescheduled and their annotations (MIG slice id / GPU device)?

maya (support): Running `kubectl describe pod` for the model pods (truncated):
```
Name: nexio-model-abc-1   Node: ded-eu2-4-nt-03   Annotations: nvidia.com/mig.gpu=1g.5gb
Name: other-tenant-rerun  Node: ded-eu2-4-nt-03   Annotations: nvidia.com/mig.gpu=1g.5gb
```
So two different tenants on same MIG slice type on same node — not expected for dedicated pool of this tenant.

sam (customer-success): Customer insists they have dedicated capacity and are seeing contention. They provided a request-id showing 503s spanning ~09:12-09:18 UTC. 

priya (eng-runtime): That lines up with noisy neighbor on the node. Looks like our scheduler allowed multiple tenant pods onto the same MIG partition class when a node restarted and autoscaler rebalanced. Temporary mitigation: cordon node and drain noisy tenant pods to other nodes, or set the nexio tenancy label to prefer exclusive packing. For immediate relief: mark `ded-eu2-4-nt-03` tainted: `kubectl taint node ded-eu2-4-nt-03 dedicated=true:NoSchedule` then untaint after eviction of other tenants.

maya (support): I ran `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` on the node at 09:16, output snippet: 
```
# gpu    sm   mem   enc   dec
000:  98   45    12   0
001:  96   42    10   0
```
That SM% is high across MIG slices.

jason (eng-sre): Confirmed. Also saw lots of KV cache eviction logs in the runtime. The combination of kubelet restart + autoscaler scaled up capacity and our packing logic assigned different tenants onto same MIG partition class. That's a policy bug.

nate (eng-infra): Short-term: I've cordoned ded-eu2-4-nt-03 and bumped pool min-size to avoid aggressive rebalancing during node rotation. I'll also add a quick scheduler predicate to prefer unique tenant per physical GPU for Dedicated pools.

priya (eng-runtime): For recovery do: 
1) bump pool min to keep stable nodes while rotation finishes
2) drain and evict pods from other tenants on that node (keep nexio pods)
3) restart model-proxy for any pods that showed 503s to clear transient states

maya (support): Executed drain of other-tenant pods at 09:28, restarted nexio model-proxy pods at 09:32, customer reported p95 dropped back to baseline by ~09:40. Customer is asking for root cause and prevention.

jason (eng-sre): Root cause hypothesis (summary to share with customer): node kubelet restart during maintenance caused autoscaler to rebalance pods; our MIG-aware scheduler allowed same MIG slice class to host multiple tenants on single physical GPU after reschedule. That produced SM saturation and KV cache thrash leading to 503s/429s.

priya (eng-runtime): Long-term fixes: enforce strict tenant-to-GPU affinity for Dedicated pools, persist MIG slice assignments across node rotations, add heuristic: if node had kubelet restart within X minutes, avoid packing different-tenants into same MIG partition class. Also add a runtime healthcheck to mitigate model-server restarts during transient GPU contention (circuit-breaker).

nate (eng-infra): Filed infra task INF-4127 to implement scheduler predicate + admission webhook to protect Dedicated pool exclusivity. Assigning to eng-infra.

maya (support): I'll follow up with customer with the summary + ETA for infra fix. Customer thanked us and asked for a postmortem when ready. :thumbsup:

jason (eng-sre): Nice quick containment. Action items: 
- eng-infra (nate) implement predicate (INF-4127)
- eng-runtime (priya) add circuit-breaker + add KV-cache telemetry alerts
- support (maya) send customer RCA and schedule follow-up.

priya (eng-runtime): I'll start a small eval job to repro MIG-misassignment in staging and capture kernel/kubelet restart sequence. If reproducible, we'll include an automated test.

nate (eng-infra): ETA for predicate + webhook: 1 sprint (2 weeks). Will share design doc here when available.

maya (support): Closing incident for now — reopened if customer sees recurrence. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
